items.content_html:
Description

Fixes 25 unbalanced or misplaced parentheses across 23 Web API pages: a missing ( or ), an extra one, or a ) that ended up inside inline code (e.g. (`currentRotation)` → (`currentRotation`)).

All changes
Page Reason
AudioBufferSourceNode/start stray opening paren before the macro, never closed
Document/getSelection extra closing paren
Element/ariaHidden extra closing paren after link
File_API/Using_files_from_web_applications extra closing paren
IDBTransaction missing closing paren
MediaRecorder parenthetical never closed
MediaStream/active '(that is, when ...' never closes
MediaStreamTrackAudioSourceNode/MediaStreamTrackAudioSourceNode '(that is, its kind property ...' never closes
PaintWorkletGlobalScope/registerPaint '(documented here on the parent class ...' never closes
PaymentResponse/retry missing closing paren
PerformanceMeasure/detail missing closing paren
Pointer_events unclosed '(when ... occurs'; the clause is the main point of the sentence, so drop the paren instead of closing it
ReadableStreamBYOBReader extra closing paren after link
Touch_events/Multi-touch_interaction extra closing paren
TrackEvent stray closing paren
Web_Audio_API/Controlling_multiple_parameters_with_ConstantSourceNode parenthetical never closed
Web_Audio_API/Controlling_multiple_parameters_with_ConstantSourceNode parenthetical never closed
Web_Audio_API/Simple_synth '(by calling our old friend addEventListener()' never closed
WebGL_API/Basic_2D_animation_example missing closing paren
WebGL_API/Basic_2D_animation_example closing paren inside inline code
WebGL_API/WebGL_best_practices extra closing paren
WebVR_API/Using_the_WebVR_API one open, two close
WebXR_Device_API/Bounded_reference_spaces extra closing paren
WebXR_Device_API/Targeting extra closing paren
XRView parenthetical '(such as ... mode' never closed

Motivation

These make sentences harder to read, especially when it's unclear where an aside ends.

Additional details

For each one, I read the whole sentence to decide whether a paren was missing or extra, and checked the git history where the intent wasn't obvious. In Pointer events, the unclosed (when a pointercancel event occurs is the main point of the sentence rather than an aside, so I removed the ( instead of closing it.

No open PR touches these files.

Related issues and pull requests

Same kind of fixes as #45998 (CSS) and #46012 (Learn).
items.title: Fix unbalanced and misplaced parentheses in Web API docs

items.content_html:
This is basically #41267, rebased on the current docs.

Since I made #41267, the notifications docs have acknowledged the difference between persistent and non-persistent notifications, but I thought there was still some clarity that could be added, and some errors still (e.g. persistent notifications are not only created from a SW, they can also be created by a web page).

One thing I wasn't sure about was whether click, close, and show are only fired on NP notifications.

Coming back to this PR, I remember why I stalled last time: the guide page https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Notifications_API/Using_the_Notifications_API needs a complete rewrite with new examples. I think the to-do list example is much too complex - I shouldn't have to understand IndexedDB to understand notifications.

I'm not proposing to do that in this PR, in the interests of finally getting it merged. But we need to do it.
items.title: Update persistent/non-persistent notifications docs

items.content_html:
Description

Update filecheck to compress JPEG, PNG, and GIF images with sharp and optimize SVGs with SVGO directly. Remove imagemin dependencies and temporary compression files.

Motivation

Simplify image compression dependencies and remove standalone binary installation scripts.

Additional details

Regression tests cover format preservation, GIF frames and timing, transparency, EXIF orientation, and file size limits.

Behavior changes compared to imagemin:

  • JPEG: mozjpeg's cjpeg reused the quality of JPEG input and kept its metadata, so it never flagged a JPEG in this repo. sharp re-encodes at quality 75 with mozjpeg optimizations and applies the EXIF orientation before stripping metadata. A full run over files/ newly flags 15 existing files (13 JPEGs, 1 PNG, 1 GIF), which CI only reports once a PR touches them.
  • GIF: gifsicle was lossless. sharp re-quantizes frames: 55 of the 58 GIFs in this repo re-encode pixel-identical, the other 3 show small colour shifts or merge a near-duplicate frame while keeping its delay, and none of them exceeds the compression threshold.

Related issues and pull requests
items.title: build(filecheck): replace imagemin with sharp

Description

Updates the size="1" paragraph in the "Accessibility concerns" section of the multiple attribute page. It no longer tells authors never to use size="1" on a multiple select, since that's now the opt-in for a drop-down multi-select. It still mentions the old behavior in browsers that haven't shipped this yet, and keeps the advice to tell users that more than one option can be selected.

Motivation

The page currently says "Don't do that" about <select multiple size="1">, which contradicts the newer HTML behavior where this markup gives a drop-down multi-select.

Additional details

  • HTML spec change: whatwg/html#11460
  • Chrome Status: https://chromestatus.com/feature/5412736871825408
  • Firefox: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1988022, WebKit: https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=309606 (and WebKit/WebKit#75555 for macOS)

I kept the sentence about browsers without support because of the interop question in the issue. Happy to drop it and just remove the paragraph if you'd prefer.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #45988

items.content_html:
Description

Reworks the onupgradeneeded handler in the IDBDatabase example so it handles upgrades from an older version, not just first-time creation:

  • The handler now checks event.oldVersion and applies each upgrade step the user hasn't had yet. Version 1 creates the toDoList store and its date/time indexes; version 2 adds the notified index to the existing store, which it gets from the upgrade transaction (DBOpenRequest.transaction.objectStore()) instead of calling createObjectStore() again.
  • The open() call asks for version 2 to match.
  • Fixes a node.appendChild typo (the variable is note), plus a missing full stop in a comment.

Motivation

As the issue says, the old handler always called createObjectStore("toDoList"), so it only worked when the database didn't exist yet. Bumping the version for anyone with an existing database threw a ConstraintError and aborted the upgrade. I checked this with fake-indexeddb: after creating the database at version 1, the old handler fails on the upgrade to version 2 with ConstraintError, while the new handler produces the same six indexes both for a fresh install at version 2 and for an upgrade from version 1.

Additional details

IndexedDB spec, IDBVersionChangeEvent.oldVersion (0 for a new database) and IDBOpenDBRequest.transaction during an upgrade.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #26638
items.title: IDBDatabase: make the upgrade example work for existing databases
